items.title: Liberals to exclude people who solely suffer from mental illness from MAID
items.excerpt: The federal government plans to indefinitely exclude people whose sole condition is mental illness from accessing medical assistance in dying, Justice Minister and Attorney General Sean Fraser said Wednesday, adding the Liberals will table legislation this fall to that effect.

items.title: Joly threatens ‘full force of the law’ over Cleveland-Cliffs’ Stelco job commitments
items.excerpt: Canada’s industry minister says Stelco Holdings Inc. cannot use the trade war to justify cutting jobs it committed to maintain when it bought the Hamilton, Ont.-based steel plant, particularly when the head of its U.S. parent company has publicly backed tariffs on steel.

items.title: Ottawa pushed to extend LGBTQ2S+ funding that is set to expire in spring
items.excerpt: Groups serving LGBTQ+ people are urging the Carney government to extend funding and programming aimed at growing mental health and security concerns.

items.title: What a separatist party’s Quebec election win means for the rest of Canada
items.excerpt: As the protracted trade war with the United States nears the two-year mark with no end in sight, two Canadian provinces could head to a vote in the next couple years on whether to separate from the federation.

items.title: Foreign influence commissioner expects registration to increase as awareness grows
items.excerpt: Canada’s foreign influence transparency commissioner suggests it’s too early to tell whether people are complying with new obligations to report information to his office.

items.title: PM Carney to again visit Turkiye later this month amid trade talks, LGBTQ2S+ crackdown
items.excerpt: Prime Minister Mark Carney is returning to Turkiye later this month as he seeks to boost trade and defence ties with a country with rising importance.

items.title: PM Carney says Canada at ‘crucial time’ in conversation with Quebec premier-designate
items.excerpt: Prime Minister Mark Carney and his cabinet ministers Tuesday pledged to work with the new separatist Parti Québécois government in Quebec through the spirit of co-operative federalism.

items.title: Martel returns to Conservative caucus, joins the Tory Senate group
items.excerpt: Quebec Sen. Richard Martel is back in the opposition caucus after joining the Conservative Senate group today.

items.title: Tom Mulcair: How Quebec voters threaded the needle to stymie the PQ’s referendum ambitions
items.excerpt: In this post-election analysis, former NDP leader Tom Mulcair breaks down Quebec's historic election night, explaining how voters threaded the needle by electing a minority PQ government to stymie referendum plans.

items.title: Don't mistake attendance at a press conference as support for a pipeline, chief says
items.excerpt: The grand chief of Treaty 8 First Nations said his presence at a pipeline press conference shouldn’t be taken as a vote of confidence.

items.title: Conservatives call for boost in Canadian diesel production, cut to diesel taxes
items.excerpt: Conservative members of Parliament are calling for a boost to Canadian diesel production to one million barrels per day as the price for the fuel continues to soar.

items.title: Should Poilievre remain as Conservative leader? Outgoing MP won’t say but insists he’s ‘doing a great job’
items.excerpt: Outgoing Conservative MP Scott Aitchison won’t say whether Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre should remain on as leader.

items.title: MPs spar over Carney’s major projects bill as Parliament returns
items.excerpt: Parliamentarians returned to Ottawa on Monday and Opposition MPs’ had their sights trained firmly on the government’s 243-page economic and labour bill.

items.title: Ottawa, Northwest Territories sign $51-million health funding agreement
items.excerpt: The federal government made the first of a series of health-care funding announcements on Monday as it works to secure seven-year deals with each of the provinces and territories. The first of those agreements, worth $51.2 million, is with the Northwest Territories.

items.title: Security screening mostly 'unimpeachable' but 'there are gaps': Anandasangaree
items.excerpt: Public Safety Minister Gary Anandasangaree acknowledged gaps in Canada’s security screening process on Monday after confirming a Canadian charged with espionage was given a security clearance.

items.title: Alberta premier unaware of reported separatist meetings with U.S. strategists
items.excerpt: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith’s office is distancing itself from one of her party presidents who met in Calgary with U.S. Republican strategists looking to assist the province’s separation movement.

items.title: Geddy Lee and Jim Cuddy have already backed candidates in Toronto’s mayoral race. Do endorsements matter?
items.excerpt: Last week, Rush frontman Geddy Lee waded into the Toronto Municipal Election campaign by making a surprise political endorsement.

items.title: B.C. Conservative leader disagrees with candidate’s anti-LGBT remarks, but won’t remove her as candidate
items.excerpt: Interim B.C. Conservative Leader Lorne Doerkson says while he doesn’t share the views expressed by the party’s candidate for Chilliwack North on LGBT issues or abortion, she will be allowed to run under the party’s banner.

items.title: Canada’s first-ever project of national interest under PM Carney revealed
items.excerpt: The Canadian government is designating a proposal for a new oil pipeline to the West Coast the first-ever project of national interest under Prime Minister Mark Carney’s Building Canada Act.
